title: Present simple: I work, she works
goal: Talk about your routine, habits and facts — and remember the -s with he/she/it.
keyPoints: Use the present simple for habits, routines and facts
I/you/we/they + verb (I work); he/she/it + verb + s (she works)
Spelling: watch → watches, study → studies, go → goes, have → has
Do not use 'be' with another verb: 'I work', never 'I am work'

explanation: We use the **present simple** for things that are **always or usually true**: routines (*I wake up at 7*), habits (*She drinks coffee every morning*) and facts (*Water boils at 100°C*).

The form is easy: **the base verb**. But with **he, she, it** (or one person/thing: *my brother, the app*) we add **-s**: I work → he work**s**. This small **-s** is the most common mistake for learners — listen for it!
**Spelling:** -ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o → add **-es** (*watches, washes, goes, does*). Consonant + y → **-ies** (*study → studies*). **have → has**.
Do not put **am/is/are** before another verb in the present simple: not *I am work* → **I work**.

rows: I live in Amman. They play football.
He lives in Cairo. She watches series.

examples.en: I get up at six and pray Fajr.
My sister studies medicine at university.
He goes to the gym three times a week.
Our team has a meeting every Sunday.
The app saves your progress in the browser.
We usually eat dinner at eight.

mistakes.why: Do not use am/is/are + verb in the present simple.

exercises.q: Our manager ___ (have) a lot of meetings.
The bus ___ (go) to the city centre.
I am drink tea in the morning.
answer: I drink tea in the morning.

exercises.q: My parents lives in a small town.
answer: My parents live in a small town.

exercises.q: every / she / walks / day / to work
answer: She walks to work every day.

script.speaker: Lina
script.text: Ahmad, what time do you start work?

script.speaker: Ahmad
script.text: I start at nine, but I get up very early, at six.

script.speaker: Lina
script.text: Six? That's early! What do you do in the morning?

script.speaker: Ahmad
script.text: I pray, I read for thirty minutes, and I have breakfast with my family.

script.speaker: Lina
script.text: Nice. My husband gets up early too. He goes to the gym before work.

script.speaker: Ahmad
script.text: And you? Do you go with him?

script.speaker: Lina
script.text: No! I sleep. I work from home, so I start at ten.

script.speaker: Ahmad
script.text: Lucky you. My office is far, so I take the bus for forty minutes.

script.speaker: Lina
script.text: The bus? My brother takes the bus too. He listens to podcasts.

script.speaker: Ahmad
script.text: Me too! I listen to English podcasts every day.

questions.q: What time does Ahmad get up?
What does Lina's husband do before work?
Why does Lina start at ten?

options: Lina's brother is take the bus.

writing.task: Describe a normal weekday for you AND for one person in your family (8–10 sentences). What time do you get up? What do you do in the morning, afternoon and evening? What does he/she do?
tips: Half of your sentences should be about 'he' or 'she' — check every -s!
Use time words: every day, usually, in the morning, at 7 o'clock.

speaking.scenario: A new friend at the gym is curious about your daily life.
speaking.aiRole: Ben, a friendly person at the gym who likes talking about daily routines
speaking.goal: Describe your routine and the routine of one family member or friend (he/she + -s). Ask Ben about his day.
speaking.starter: Hey! I see you here a lot. So, what does a normal day look like for you?
